papers.title: Turtle watcher's note
lines: The turtles come up the beach at night, heavy, patient, three hundred pounds of bad temper.
They dig, they lay, they weep, they return. Do not use a torch. Do not offer advice.

papers.title: Cable station log
lines: The undersea cable runs from here to Cape Town and to Britain. We pass the news, we do not read it.
Sometimes the dots and dashes spell something rude. We keep that to ourselves.

papers.title: Gardener's note
lines: Green Mountain is a cloud forest in the middle of a desert, planted by hand by sailors and botanists.
They brought the first seeds in a ship in the 1800s. Now it drips.

papers.title: Airfield memo
lines: The terns on the airfield are called Wideawake, from the noise they make at night.
They are right to be. There are a great many of them, and one runway.

trail.clue: An engineer buried a flask near the big rock 'for the day the terns leave'.
